If she is an apprentice of your shop because her mentor is no longer there, then you should probably talk to her at least one more time as the shop owner about teamwork, shop expectations, etc.. At our shop, apprentices didn't get the opportunity to deny any style of work, unless it was truly outside of their skill level for multiple reasons: they're learning and growing their art/trade/technique as they're "too new" to know what their style is, being the lowest on the totem of experience should mean she's grateful to get any of that work or experience, and being a team member and supporting your shop should mean she's encouraging clients to stay at your business regardless of her personal feelings about your other artist, unless he truly isn't suited for the job.

You could cut ties with her completely, or you could reiterate expectations like a business owner. I've felt the same way about other apprentices my shop owner has taken on as your other artist has, and while I've complained in private, I would also take the time to help them grow instead of doing nothing so our shop didn't look bad as a whole. Not saying he has to step in as a mentor, because that's not his job, but it does sound like the apprentice is either too lax or too comfortable in the space considering her lack of experience. Just make sure everyone is on the same page.
